title: GPU allocator churn bailout causing KV index jitter and fragmentation across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Maya Patel
description: Summary: Multiple customers reported sudden GPU OOMs and elevated latency during tenant surge events over the last week. Symptoms: OOMs during long-context generation, asymmetric memory reclaim on dedicated nodes, and downstream KV cache index inconsistencies that manifested as corrupted session handles. Scope: Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and one Private on-prem deployment. Immediate impact: customer request failures, degraded throughput, and at least two Sev1 escalations. This ticket tracks triage, mitigations, root-cause analysis, and a runtime patch + rollout plan.
timeline: 2026-03-08: First alert from hosted region us-west-2 (reduced capacity, OOM spikes). 2026-03-09: Dedicated customer A opened support case with reproducible OOM during long-chat sessions. 2026-03-10: Private customer B reported memory corruption observed in KV index checksums after heavy prefix cache churn. 2026-03-11: On-call merged emergency throttle to reduce burst concurrency (short-term mitigation). 2026-03-12: Engineering reproduced deterministic fragmentation using synthetic workload locally. 2026-03-13: Prototype allocator bailout + index stitcher patch created. 2026-03-14: Canary rollout to a small subset of hosted nodes; passed basic smoke tests. 2026-03-15: This ticket updated with canary results and plan for broader rollout.
impact: High-impact — multiple customers experienced failed requests and increased latency; two customers escalated to enterprise success teams. Observed across deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private). Intermittent but repeatable with heavy multi-tenant churn and sequences > 8k tokens. Some nodes entered unrecoverable OOM states requiring instance replacement.
root_cause: Concurrency between the GPU allocator's fast-path reclaim (a heuristic 'bailout' that attempts to free ephemeral arenas) and the KV cache index delta-apply path led to a race. Under sustained churn this produced fragmented arenas and stale index references; subsequent compaction attempts would double-free or leave tombstoned entries that made session handles invalid. The allocator's heuristics were tuned for throughput but failed to enforce strict ordering of metadata updates vs. physical block reuse on preemptible GPU kernels, exposing a memory-safety window that escalated to OOMs.
immediate_mitigation: 1) Rate-limit burst concurrency for affected customers in hosted regions (applied by infra runbooks). 2) Increase per-tenant soft memory quota on Dedicated nodes to force earlier eviction rather than allocator bailout. 3) Temporary guard in runtime to refuse 'fast-path free' when KV index delta is active (deployed as livepatch v1.0.1 to canary). 4) Manual session sweep for Private customer B to rebuild corrupted index and restore service.
long_term_fix: 1) Introduce ordered write barrier: allocator must publish block retirement only after KV index delta commit completes. 2) Replace heuristic bailout with bounded compaction that yields to KV index operations. 3) Add checksum-and-epoch metadata to KV index updates so stale references are detected and rejected instead of used. 4) Add a background compactor that incrementally defragments arenas without blocking request path. Target release: runtime-1.20. Estimated engineering effort: 3 sprints.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Canary): deploy livepatch v1.0.1 (fast guard) to 2% hosted fleet and one dedicated pool; monitor for 48 hours. Phase 1 (Staged): deploy allocator bailguard + index stitcher v1.0.3 to 25% fleet + all dedicated test pools; run synthetic churn test jobs. Phase 2 (Gradual): expand to 75% with automated rollback on error. Phase 3 (Full): ship runtime-1.20 with compactor and full fixes; ramp to 100% with post-deploy regression evaluation against historical prompt suites. Private customers: provide patch bundle and runbook; offer on-site validation for enterprise customers. Rollback: if OOM rate exceeds baseline + 10% over 1h, automatically revert to prior runtime binary and throttle bursts.
canary_strategy: Select canary hosts from low-risk tenant sets with traffic mirrors enabled. Use two independent canaries: one hosted multi-tenant and one dedicated single-tenant pool. Run 12h synthetic long-context generator with concurrent short queries. Key metrics: OOM_count, allocator_free_latency, kv_index_error_rate, end-to-end p95 latency, per-tenant token throughput. Canary success criteria: OOM_count == 0 and kv_index_error_rate <= baseline for 48h.
test_plan: Unit tests for ordered write barrier and checksum verification. Integration tests: reproduce fragmentation with synthetic churn harness and verify session recovery. Regression bench: run pre- and post-patch perf tests across model families (decoder-only and encoder-decoder) for sequences 512, 2048, 8192. Chaos tests: simulate kernel preemptions and GPU driver delays to validate safety nets. Add a new workload in nightly CI that reproduces the tenant surge pattern for future regressions.
monitoring_and_alerting: New alerts: allocator-bailout-invocations > 0 for > 5m, kv-index-checksum-mismatch > 1/min, gpu-memory-sudden-drop-and-oom > 1 in 10m. Dashboards updated to show per-tenant allocator churn heatmap and kv-index-latency percentiles. Alert routing: Pager to runtime-oncall, Slack notification to #runtime-stability, email to customer success for enterprise customers. Post-deploy: collect detailed heap profiles on any node that triggers OOM and upload to S3 for triage.
customer_updates: 2026-03-10: Sent initial acknowledgment to affected customers with short-term throttling actions (Support-#12345).
2026-03-13: Provided ETA for patch and offered Dedicated customers a temporary capacity bump to reduce risk.
2026-03-15: Shared canary success summary and next steps; scheduled migration window for enterprise Private customers.
notes: Decisions: prefer conservative correctness-first approach for allocator ordering; performance optimizations can follow after we restore reliability. Keep Dedicated and Private customers on optional early rollout channel for extra validation. Follow-ups: add per-tenant memory telemetry to detect harmful allocation patterns and surface to customers as a cost/quality signal. Ensure legal/regulatory teams are notified for any Private customer that requires binary changes under change-control.
